Q: Looking for a data viewer in Visual Studio Code similar to RStudio's A:

You can use Jupyter Notebooks within VS Code to get a similar interface to the one you highlighted in RStudio.

See the panel at the bottom here

To create a Jupyter Notebook simply create a file with type .ipynb then VS Code should prompt you to install the appropriate (Microsoft provided) extensions.

To view the pane at the bottom of the screen you can use the ctrl + j shortcut (cmd + j on Mac) or simply select the "Jupyter" tab if the bottom pane is already open. The "Jupyter Variables" button near the top of the screen also works to do the same thing.

As for exploring a dataframe loaded into memory, you may find useful Microsoft's Data Wrangler extension (Getting Started Guide).

Q: Is scalar fmov guaranteed to clear the upper lanes to 0? A:

This documentation for the AArch64 architecture specifies the semantics of the FMOV instruction, in its register-to-register variant, include:

var result : bits(128) = Zeros{};

which sets all 128 bits of result to zeros, and then:

result[0+:esize] = operand;

The +: is a slice operator, which is defined in ARM’s insanely formal specification of their specification language, Architecture Specification Language Reference. Quite simply, a+:b is a field of bits starting at bit number a, with a field length of b bits. So result[0+:esize] = operand; sets the first esize bits of result to the value of the instruction operand. esize is the number of bits for the data type of the instruction (16, 32, or 64 bits for half-, single-, or double-precision).

After that, the result is written to the destination register:

V{128}(d) = result;

So, all bits beyond the first esize bits are set to zero.

Q: Redshift: Numeric data overflow (result precision) A:
  1. try to check the what is the type of the column you are going to insert
  2. use the type in the value you insert.

According to my understanding, the error means that the type of value that you want to insert is different with the type of value in the column.

For example, you cannot inset 1.3333 into a column with only one-digit value like 1.3.

Q: error: command 'cl.exe' failed: No such file or directory Python 3.4 A:

Python 3.4 requires Visual Studio 2010 to compile packages like pyodbc, so if you have a different version installed that's definitely the problem. Simply reinstall Visual Studio and everything should work fine! https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=23691 If you still have problems consider changing to 3.5 or 3.6 which will soon come out!

Hope it helped, Stam

Q: How to customize date format when creating excel cells through javascript (activexobject)? A:

In Vbscript, we use to resolve this by

    If IsDate ( Cell.Value ) Then
         Cell.Value = DateValue ( Cell.Value )
    End If

Maybe, In java script also you need to play with same approach.

Q: Why does ordering a tree-model chart DESC make M4 choose different sampled points? A:

These results suggest that M4 builds its windows in scan order in 2.0.8. Adding ORDER BY TIME DESC therefore changes which timestamps receive a sample; it is not just reversing an already sampled result. If the chart needs stable samples, run M4 with ascending input and reverse the rows in the application, and record this as a version-specific behavior.
